newsitem.title: GREECE: KAKLAMANIS FAILS TO WIN PARL PRESIDENCY ON 1ST BALLOT.
newsitem.headline: KAKLAMANIS FAILS TO WIN PARL PRESIDENCY ON 1ST BALLOT.

text.p: Apostolos Kaklamanis, from the ruling socialist party, failed to win re-election as Greek parliamentary president on the first ballot on Tuesday, parliamentary officials said.
Kaklamanis, elected parliamentary president in October 1993 when the socialists returned to power, received 150 votes on the first ballot -- one short of the required 151 for election.
The socialists won 162 deputies in the 300-seat parliament in early elections in September. Officials said there were 160 socialists present for the vote. A second ballot was being hastily organised.
Conservative opposition candidate Anna Psarouda-Benaki got 95 votes in the first round. The conservative party has 108 deputies in parliament. --Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
